title: 29-layer HfO2/MgF2 UV bandpass with relaxed thickness bounds and best-candidate initialization
scientific_hypothesis: The optimal 29-layer HfO2/MgF2 bandpass filter for 255-280 nm transmission has at least one layer thickness between 25-30 nm; relaxing the lower bound from 30 nm to 25 nm and initializing from the historical best configuration will improve the target score beyond 0.738.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory suggests that layer thicknesses near λ/4n at the center wavelength create constructive interference in the passband. For UV at ~267 nm center, HfO2 (n~2.1-2.3 in UV) gives ~29-32 nm quarter-wave thickness, and MgF2 (n~1.38-1.42 in UV) gives ~47-48 nm. Some layers in a multi-band design may need to deviate from exact quarter-wave to balance multiple spectral regions, potentially requiring thicknesses below 30 nm.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | SiO2 substrate (29 coating layers, alternating HfO2 first from air)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 29 coating layers, optimization bounds [25, 150] nm
Initialization from historical best candidate thicknesses with ±5 nm perturbation
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 29 (under 30-layer limit)
All materials are conventional evaporable or sputterable dielectrics
Minimum thickness 25 nm is near the lower limit for uniform deposition control
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: HfO2 has refractive index approximately 2.1-2.3 in the 250-300 nm UV range, making it a suitable high-index material for UV bandpass filters
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has refractive index approximately 1.38-1.42 in the UV range and is one of the lowest-index conventional dielectric coatings available
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave optical thickness at 267 nm center wavelength gives physical thickness of λ/4n, approximately 29-32 nm for HfO2 and 47-48 nm for MgF2
Recalled knowledge: Alternating high-low index stacks create stopbands centered at the quarter-wave wavelength, with bandwidth scaling with index contrast ratio
Recalled knowledge: Multi-band suppression (visible and NIR) requires either multiple stack periods or non-quarter-wave layer thicknesses to create additional stopband features
expected_advantages: Relaxing the 30 nm lower bound to 25 nm may allow the optimizer to find thinner layers that better balance the three spectral bands
Initializing from the historical best (score 0.738) with small perturbations focuses the search near a known good solution rather than random exploration
29 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for multi-band control while staying under the 30-layer manufacturing constraint
known_risks: I am uncertain about the exact UV refractive index values of HfO2 and MgF2 at 255-280 nm; the material catalog datasets will provide measured values
I am uncertain whether 25 nm minimum thickness is practically depositable with uniform control; this would need process validation
I do not know if the historical best candidate at 0.738 is near a global optimum or a local maximum; this route tests only local improvement
The alternating HfO2/MgF2 topology is fixed; if a different material pair or non-alternating sequence would perform better, this route cannot discover it
I am recalling that MgF2 is UV-transparent down to ~115 nm, but the exact extinction coefficient behavior in 255-280 nm band should be verified from the dataset
execution_request_english: Design a 29-layer planar multilayer filter on a SiO2 (Gao) substrate with air incidence. The stack alternates HfO2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) starting with HfO2 from the air side: HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) | HfO2 | SiO2 (Gao) substrate. Optimize all 29 coating layer thicknesses with bounds [25, 150] nm. Initialize thicknesses from the historical best candidate (thicknesses: [115.0, 140.5, 112.5, 70.0, 51.0, 83.0, 126.0, 97.5, 158.5, 107.5, 60.0, 72.5, 64.5, 103.0, 77.0, 89.5, 89.0, 178.0, 95.0, 182.0, 105.5, 86.5, 99.5, 175.5, 57.5, 96.5, 95.5, 77.5, 103.0] nm) with ±5 nm random perturbation. Use coherent transfer matrix method solver. Evaluate three spectral bands: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. No metal layers. Total coating layers exactly 29.
revision_reason: Continuation of control route: relaxed lower thickness bound from 30 nm to 25 nm per feedback directive, changed initialization from uniform random to targeted perturbation around historical best candidate (target_score 0.738) to test whether optimal solution lies just outside previous bounds
